question.problem:
The projection of the intersection between the elliptic paraboloid $4(x-1)^{2}+25(y+1)^{2}=100(z-2)$ and the plane 
$z=7$  onto the $xy$-plane is an ellipse. What are the lengths of the semi-axes of the ellipse?
question.worked_solution:
To find the intersection of the paraboloid and the plane $z=7$, we substitute $z=7$ into the equation of the paraboloid, and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}4(x-1)^{2}+25(y+1)^{2}=100(z-2) \\ 4(x-1)^{2}+25(y+1)^{2}=100(7-2) \\ 4(x-1)^{2}+25(y+1)^{2}=500 \\ \frac{(x-1)^{2}}{125}+\frac{(y+1)^{2}}{20} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-1)^{2}}{(5\sqrt{5})^{2}}+\frac{(y+1)^{2}}{(2\sqrt{5})^{2}} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us the equation of an ellipse with semi-axes of lengths $5\sqrt{5}$ and $2\sqrt{5}.$
